None establishes a personal command, escalation, concealment, or independently verified presidential risk reduction.","closed_system_silence":"Information constraints, including Papua restrictions, show that silence could conceal misconduct, but no nuclear-specific transparency audit or concealed-conduct evidence is supplied.","duplicate_reporting":"RC021-RC024 share BAPETEN as a reporting gateway, and RC002, RC021, and RC022 may overlap on safeguards. Counts must remain locator- and claim-specific.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both favorable safeguards, protection, and cyber-governance evidence and adverse audit evidence were searched. The remaining attribution gap appears constrained by the bounded accessible 2022 source trail.","missing_source_type":"No directly attributable presidential nuclear-policy, command-and-control, escalation, or independently verified safety-outcome source is available; this appears access- and domain-constrained.","official_claim_independence":"IAEA and U.S. assessment involvement provide some external checking, but most continuation evidence is official or official-relay material and does not independently verify efficacy or presidential ownership.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Complaint volume is not a meaningful safety measure in this specialized domain; few public complaints would not establish safety.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"SIPRI and IAEA establish national exposure and inherited baseline; RC025-RC026 establish formal authority. RC007 reports contested Papua violence involving state and non-state actors. These cannot establish presidential responsibility without orders, knowledge, tolerance, or remedy evidence.","closed_system_silence":"Papua information restrictions can suppress reporting on civilian harm, security conduct, and accountability; official silence cannot be read as absence of misconduct.","duplicate_reporting":"Ukraine, Myanmar, and Papua reporting may describe overlapping underlying events. Reused IDs are appropriate, but repeated coverage must not inflate source-claim counts.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Favorable diplomatic and peace-effort evidence and adverse Papua/conflict material were both searched. Orders, rules of engagement, arms end-use, and accountability searches remain research-recoverable gaps.","missing_source_type":"Primary civilian-protection directives, rules of engagement, arms-recipient/end-use records, field reporting, and accountability or remedy records are missing.","official_claim_independence":"RC003 is an external official diplomatic record; RC006 and RC020 are Indonesian official accounts establishing actions or statements, not efficacy. RC004 and RC005 provide external analytical or media checks.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Open reporting can make accessible incidents appear more prevalent, while Papua restrictions suppress visibility; complaint and conflict-reporting volume cannot establish severity or prevalence.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"LF073-LF076 and military-spending records establish exposure and baseline; state/non-state responsibility, subnational authority, inherited conflict, COVID recovery, and Ukraine-related shocks remain insufficiently separated.","supporting_evidence_ids":["RC003","RC004","RC005","RC006","RC007","RC020","RC028","RC029","RC030","RC031","RC032","LF073","LF076","LS042","LS043"],"unresolved_risks":["Papua civilian-protection and remedy attribution remains incomplete.","Diplomatic activity is better evidenced than outcomes, correction, or accountability.","Local-language and primary security documentation is absent."]},"chapter_id":"2B","defensible_evidence_estimate":10,"independent_source_family_estimate":8,"missing_themes":["Civilian-protection orders and rules of engagement","Arms recipients and end-use accountability","Independent Papua accountability and remedy evidence","Contrary evidence on diplomatic effectiveness"],"substantive_issues":["Contested state/non-state conduct cannot be attributed automatically to Widodo.","The continuation added contrary diplomatic-efficacy and Papua institutional evidence but did not recover primary security or remedy records.","Further bounded research could materially improve attribution and event coverage."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"RC008-RC013 and RC033-RC038 distinguish external reporting, NGO assessments, documented institutional actions, legal provisions, trial outcomes, and formal remedy initiatives. Alleged abuses remain distinct from adjudicated findings; RC037 explicitly preserves legal uncertainty.","closed_system_silence":"Papua restrictions, surveillance, harassment, and constrained journalism could conceal abuse, prison conditions, vulnerable-group harms, and failed remedies.","duplicate_reporting":"HRW, Amnesty, Freedom House, RSF, Human Rights Monitor, and local indicators may repeat common incidents or trends. Stable IDs help, but underlying-fact reconciliation remains necessary.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Adverse rights evidence and favorable evidence of continuing media and civil-society operation were both searched. Presidential rhetoric, remedy effectiveness, prison conditions, vulnerable-group protection, and primary corroboration remain research-recoverable gaps.","missing_source_type":"Primary court, prison, police/military disciplinary, remedy, vulnerable-group, and local-language records are missing.","official_claim_independence":"RC008 and RC033-RC034 provide external official reporting; RC009-RC013 and RC035-RC038 provide NGO, monitoring, and legal checks. No systematic independent verification of government denials or remedy implementation is supplied.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Open NGO and media reporting can increase visible complaint volume, while Papua restrictions and surveillance suppress reporting. Volume cannot serve as a prevalence denominator.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Local and longitudinal indicators establish population exposure and baseline; executive, security, judicial, legislative, and subnational authority, plus COVID and Papua shocks, are not fully disentangled.","supporting_evidence_ids":["RC007","RC008","RC009","RC010","RC011","RC012","RC013","RC033","RC034","RC035","RC036","RC037","RC038","LF322","LF331","LF440","LF445","LS003","LS011"],"unresolved_risks":["Direct presidential knowledge, tolerance, correction, and remedy effectiveness are unevenly evidenced.","The Criminal Code evidence spans 2019 and 2022 and requires strict temporal separation.","Prison and vulnerable-group evidence remains materially incomplete."]},"chapter_id":"3B","defensible_evidence_estimate":13,"independent_source_family_estimate":8,"missing_themes":["Direct presidential rhetoric or incitement","Remedy and accountability effectiveness","Prison conditions","Vulnerable-group protection","Independent primary corroboration"],"substantive_issues":["Country-level rights indicators cannot establish personal attribution.","The continuation materially improved event-level, accountability, and remedy coverage but left important population and primary-source gaps.","Further bounded research could improve the selected lenses."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"RC011-RC013 and RC040-RC045 distinguish comparative assessments, reported pressure, formal legislative acts, legal analysis, and official claims. The election-delay controversy and institutional influence remain incompletely sourced and should not be presented as established personal conduct.","closed_system_silence":"Papua, surveillance, defamation pressure, and constrained journalism could conceal executive influence, electoral manipulation, or institutional noncompliance.","duplicate_reporting":"Freedom House, RSF, HRW, and local indicators may overlap on the same incidents or trends. Only distinct source-locator-claim units should count.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Competitive political space and independent media were considered alongside restrictions and manipulation. Primary searches for the election-delay controversy, election-institution influence, Criminal Code implementation, and corrective evidence remain incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Primary election-administration, parliamentary, court, presidential-statement, implementation-guidance, and local-monitoring sources are missing.","official_claim_independence":"Formal official records establish acts but do not validate institutional independence or implementation. NGO assessments offer external checks but may share reporting ecosystems; RC044 provides balanced comparative checking.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Open complaints and media coverage may increase visible deterioration, while surveillance and pressure suppress complaints. No denominator or complaint-volume audit is supplied.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Local indicators address institutional baseline and exposure, but executive, legislative, judicial, electoral, and subnational authority are not fully separated; COVID-era conditions affect comparisons.","supporting_evidence_ids":["RC011","RC012","RC013","RC040","RC041","RC042","RC043","RC044","RC045","LF616","LF623","LF884","LF898","LS010","LS015","LS021","LS044","LS046"],"unresolved_risks":["Primary evidence for the election-delay controversy is explicitly incomplete.","Criminal Code implementation and executive influence lack sufficient event-level documentation.","Positive institutional context and corrective evidence are underdeveloped."]},"chapter_id":"4B","defensible_evidence_estimate":11,"independent_source_family_estimate":7,"missing_themes":["Primary evidence on the election-delay controversy","Executive influence over election institutions","Criminal Code implementation and enforcement","Independent evidence of institutional correction or remedy"],"substantive_issues":["Comparative indices and NGO assessments require precise locator and attribution controls.","The continuation added direct legislative-process evidence and balanced institutional material but did not resolve election-delay or implementation gaps.","Further bounded research is likely to recover primary and contrary evidence."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"RC014-RC019 and RC046-RC051 separate macroeconomic outcomes, technical assessments, project and fiscal-reform approvals, audit coverage, distributional findings, and formal appointment authority. Growth is not a finding of ruler effectiveness, and governance weaknesses are not automatically personal failures.","closed_system_silence":"Subnational and institutional weaknesses may conceal procurement, distribution, and service-delivery failures not visible in macroeconomic reporting.","duplicate_reporting":"World Bank material is reused across chapters and lenses. Page- or box-level locators and distinct underlying claims are necessary to avoid inflated counts.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Recovery, appointments, and policy activity were searched alongside inflation, tax, infrastructure, distribution, and social-protection weaknesses. Appointment-to-outcome linkage, project implementation, and subnational evidence remain incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Procurement and audit findings at project level, completion and distribution data, subnational reporting, beneficiary evidence, and independent evaluation of appointments are missing.","official_claim_independence":"RC019 establishes appointment authority and RC046 establishes a formal reform action, but neither proves outcomes. World Bank analysis offers a technical check, while RC048 supplies audit-system evidence; both retain coverage and official-data limitations.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Beneficiary and service complaints may be more visible in open or monitored regions and less visible in marginalized regions; complaint volume is not a severity measure.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"World Bank and local indicators address outcomes, inequality, baseline governance, and exposure. Learning loss and human-development indicators are outcomes, not personal findings.","closed_system_silence":"Regional inequality, incomplete coverage, and weak monitoring may conceal service failures and exclusion, especially for populations with limited access or reporting capacity.","duplicate_reporting":"World Bank project, human-capital, and COVID materials support distinct claims but need locator reconciliation. Local indicators are structured context, not automatically independent narrative sources.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Policy activity and long-term gains were considered alongside learning loss, uneven quality, incomplete coverage, and inequality. Affordability, quality, regional distribution, political conditionality, and target-year recovery response remain incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Household and beneficiary surveys, school and health administrative records, independent program evaluations, local-language reporting, and regional affordability/distribution data are missing.","official_claim_independence":"World Bank records provide external analysis but may rely on government data. Project approval establishes intended action and design, not realized impact or equitable delivery; RC055-RC056 add independent methodological and implementation checks.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Service complaints may be more visible in open systems while underserved regions and vulnerable groups are underreported. Complaint volume lacks a denominator and cannot measure severity.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"HDI and health/education indicators address population outcomes and baseline; donor, subnational, inherited, and COVID-shock contributions remain material, with shared delivery authority.","supporting_evidence_ids":["RC016","RC017","RC018","RC052","RC053","RC054","RC055","RC056","RC057","LF1325","LF1333","LF1023","LF1025","LS039","LS047","LS048"],"unresolved_risks":["Target-year affordability, quality, and regional distribution evidence is thin.","Donor and subnational contributions complicate attribution.","Policy alignment and project approval are not outcome evidence."]},"chapter_id":"6B","defensible_evidence_estimate":9,"independent_source_family_estimate":5,"missing_themes":["Affordability and coverage by population","Service quality and regional distribution","Independent evaluation of human-capital programs","Political conditionality or exclusion","Target-period post-shock recovery response"],"substantive_issues":["National human-development indicators remain insufficient to establish ruler-specific delivery quality.","The continuation added recovery-response, methodological, and implementation evidence but left material population and regional gaps.","Further bounded research could materially improve the selected lenses."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"RC010-RC013 and RC058-RC062 document disclosures, institutional weakening, reported pressure, formal legal developments, audits, and attributed civil-society allegations. They do not establish Widodo’s personal enrichment, family benefit, deliberate deception, knowledge, or direct obstruction. RC063 is unresolved, not adverse evidence.","closed_system_silence":"Weakening oversight, pressure on monitors, and intimidation can conceal corruption, favoritism, conflicts, and obstruction; silence is especially non-probative in this chapter.","duplicate_reporting":"KPK, civil-society, legal, and press reports may repeat one institutional episode or campaign. The notebook still has limited precise locators for the personal nexus, so duplicate underlying facts are a material risk.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Adverse institutional-integrity evidence and favorable disclosure/safeguard material were both searched. Direct beneficial-ownership, conflict, knowledge, intervention, and corrective-action searches remain incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Beneficial-ownership and conflict-of-interest records, audit and court findings tied to personal conduct, investigative local journalism, and direct evidence of presidential knowledge or intervention are missing.","official_claim_independence":"RC058-RC059 provide disclosure records and RC061 audit-system evidence; RC060 is a favorable official safeguard claim. These do not independently establish honesty or implementation. RC062 is an attributed civil-society allegation rather than an adjudicated finding.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Repeated complaints against monitors may exaggerate apparent hostility if they reflect one campaign; intimidation and weakened oversight may suppress corruption complaints. Volume is unreliable in either direction.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Country corruption indicators establish institutional baseline, not personal conduct. Shared authority, inherited KPK conditions, and political or institutional shocks are not fully separated from the ruler’s personal nexus.","supporting_evidence_ids":["RC010","RC011","RC012","RC013","RC019","RC058","RC059","RC060","RC061","RC062","LF1406","LF1409","LS012","LS013","LS022","LS065"],"unresolved_risks":["Personal-integrity nexus remains unresolved.","No verified evidence of personal enrichment, family benefit, deliberate deception, or direct obstruction is established.","Institutional weakening and civil-society attribution cannot be converted into personal dishonesty without additional evidence."]},"chapter_id":"7B","defensible_evidence_estimate":8,"independent_source_family_estimate":7,"missing_themes":["Personal enrichment or family benefit","Conflict-of-interest and beneficial-ownership evidence","Direct presidential obstruction or knowledge","Integrity disclosures and audit findings tied to personal conduct","Contrary evidence of personal safeguards or corrective action"],"substantive_issues":["Chapter 7B requires a personal-integrity nexus, which remains unestablished.","The continuation added disclosure and audit material but did not resolve personal attribution or contrary safeguards.","Further bounded research could recover personal/network integrity records and investigative evidence."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"RC005-RC006, RC014-RC020, and RC064-RC069 distinguish formal actions, project records, technical assessments, measured outcomes, implementation monitoring, and efficacy limitations. Official success claims are not treated as independent findings; RC066 and RC069 provide contrary evaluation evidence.","closed_system_silence":"Papua and weak subnational or institutional monitoring may conceal implementation failure, exclusion, uncorrected harms, and failed diplomatic or security feedback.","duplicate_reporting":"World Bank and official records are reused across lenses. Distinct locators and source-claim units are required, especially where several IDs concern one program or diplomatic action.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Attributable programs, implementation weaknesses, external-shock dependence, and mixed diplomatic effectiveness were all searched. Adaptation, correction, durable results, distributional effects, and independent diplomatic assessment remain incompletely searched.","missing_source_type":"Independent project evaluations, audit and procurement records, beneficiary and subnational evidence, implementation tracking, diplomatic outcome assessments, and local-language reporting are missing.","official_claim_independence":"Cabinet statements and project records establish action or intent. World Bank analysis and evaluation supply some external checking, but official-data dependence and limited target-period outcome evidence remain material.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Visible complaints and NGO reporting may overstate severity in open settings, while Papua and weak monitoring suppress complaints. Neither complaint volume nor official silence reliably measures effectiveness.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"World Bank and local facts address national outcomes and governance baseline. its remaining attribution and independent-efficacy gap is credibly constrained, so it does not require another search round.","Chapters 2B-8B received continuation evidence, including contrary material and additional primary or independent checks, but each retains a concrete research-recoverable gap in attribution, remedy, implementation, distribution, personal nexus, or outcome verification.","Across chapters, official claims are generally separated from independent findings, but gateway reuse, source-family overlap, and locator-level deduplication remain deterministic handoff risks.","Local facts are explicitly used as contextual baselines and are not treated as ruler-attributed evidence; missing evidence is not treated as negative ruler evidence.","No scores, score ranges, anchors, rankings, or judge-directed recommendations were assigned."],"needs_continuation":true,"reviewer_summary":"Chapter 1B is adequately bounded for this review and should remain unresolved for confidence because attribution and independent efficacy are limited, but another broad search is unlikely to materially improve it. Chapters 2B-8B require continuation within the selected lens scope: concrete recoverable gaps remain in security attribution and remedy, rights remedies and vulnerable-group coverage, election and legal implementation, economic delivery and distribution, human-development quality and regional access, personal integrity nexus, and effectiveness correction and outcome evaluation. These gaps constrain evidence interpretation; they are not adverse ruler evidence.","schema_version":"ruler_evidence_review_v1","selected_theme_ids":["2B","3B","4B","5B","6B","7B","8B"]}
